record.original_question: Fix d in N and epsilon in (0,1). What is the least k = k(d,epsilon) such that every degree-d polynomial threshold event over a k-wise independent Gaussian-marginal random vector X approximates the corresponding event under a standard Gaussian vector Z within additive error epsilon; that is, |Pr[p(X) >= 0] - Pr[p(Z) >= 0]| <= epsilon for every degree-d polynomial p : R^n -> R?

evidence.quote: Statement: Fix d in N and epsilon in (0, 1). Determine the least k = k( d, epsilon) such that the following holds: If p : R^n -> R is any degree- d multivariate polynomial, and X is any R^n-valued random variable with the property that each X_i has the standard Gaussian distribution and each collection X_{i1}, ..., X_{ik} is independent, then | Pr[ p( X ) >= 0] - Pr[ p( Z ) >= 0]| <= epsilon, where Z has the standard n-dimensional Gaussian distribution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ be fixed. For an integer $n \geq 1$, call a random vector $X = (X_1, \ldots, X_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ a $k$-wise independent Gaussian-marginal vector if (i) each coordinate $X_i$ has the standard Gaussian distribution $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, and (ii) every subset of $k$ distinct coordinates $X_{i_1}, \ldots, X_{i_k}$ is mutually independent (so its joint law is the standard $k$-dimensional Gaussian). Let $Z = (Z_1, \ldots, Z_n)$ denote a fully independent standard $n$-dimensional Gaussian vector.

Determine the least integer $k = k(d, \varepsilon)$ with the following property: for every $n \geq 1$, every degree-$d$ multivariate polynomial $p : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, and every $k$-wise independent Gaussian-marginal vector $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\bigl| \Pr[p(X) \geq 0] - \Pr[p(Z) \geq 0] \bigr| \leq \varepsilon.$$

In particular, give matching upper and lower bounds on $k(d,\varepsilon)$ as a function of $d$ and $\varepsilon$.
artifact.category_tag: bounded independence and polynomial threshold functions
artifact.status_search_result: Upper bounds on k(d,ε) for Gaussian polynomial threshold functions of arbitrary degree d were established by Kane (CCC 2011, "k-Independent Gaussians Fool Polynomial Threshold Functions"), with quantitative improvements in subsequent work, but the tight value of k(d,ε)—matching upper and lower bounds as a function of d and ε—remains unresolved in the literature. Known bounds are polynomial in 1/ε for fixed d (with various exponents depending on d) and do not match known lower bounds, so the problem of determining the exact least k(d,ε) is still open.

status_evidence.title: k-Independent Gaussians Fool Polynomial Threshold Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that k-wise independent Gaussians fool degree-d PTFs for k = poly(d, 1/ε), but does not establish matching lower bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bound exists; tight value unknown.

status_evidence.title: Bounded Independence Fools Degree-2 Threshold Functions
status_evidence.snippet: For degree-2 PTFs, k = poly(1/ε) suffices; the precise polynomial exponent is not pinned down to be tight.
status_evidence.claim: Even for d=2 the optimal exponent in 1/ε is not fully determined.

status_evidence.title: A Pseudorandom Generator for Functions of Low-Degree Polynomial Threshold Functions (ICALP 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to improve pseudorandom generators / bounded independence parameters for PTFs, indicating tight bounds remain unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Continued research suggests problem is still open.
